items.title: Transport soak coverage set
items.statement: ATS-021 requires soak coverage for sleep/wake, reconnect, first-event timeout, large terminal output, high-frequency browser snapshots, and WebSocket fallback.

evidence.exact_quote: - Sleep/wake, reconnect, first-event timeout, large terminal output, high-frequency browser snapshots, and WebSocket fallback are covered.

items.title: Transport soak oracles are unspecified
items.statement: The coverage assertion does not define soak duration, connection/load profile, first-event timeout threshold, snapshot frequency, output size, observable metrics, expected fallback path, or pass/fail criteria, so independent builders cannot implement or certify the same soak suite.
items.impact: Transport regressions can pass or fail according to builder-selected thresholds and workloads.
items.builder_discretion: Select every quantitative workload, threshold, observation, and oracle for ATS-021.

evidence.exact_quote: - Sleep/wake, reconnect, first-event timeout, large terminal output, high-frequency browser snapshots, and WebSocket fallback are covered.

items.title: Permanent minimized terminal replay corpus
items.statement: ATS-022 requires minimized replay fixtures spanning parser bugs, shell markers, giant output, Unicode/graphemes, bracketed paste, OSC, multiplexed and SSH panes, and CLI agents.

evidence.exact_quote: - PM stores minimized terminal replay fixtures for parser bugs, shell markers, giant outputs, unicode/graphemes, bracketed paste, OSC, tmux/zellij/ssh panes, and CLI agents.

items.title: Terminal replay comparison surfaces
items.statement: Terminal fuzzing, chunk splitting, and replay snapshots must compare the parse tree, accessible mirror, scrollback, and painted viewport.

evidence.exact_quote: - Terminal parser has fuzz tests, chunk-splitting tests, and replay snapshots that compare parse tree, accessible mirror, scrollback, and painted viewport.

items.title: Oversized recording graceful degradation
items.statement: Oversized terminal recordings must degrade with receipts rather than freezing the UI.

evidence.exact_quote: - Renderer/scrollback locks are budgeted; oversized recordings degrade with receipts instead of freezing UI.

items.title: Terminal performance and degradation budgets are absent
items.statement: The requirement says locks are budgeted and oversized recordings degrade, but supplies no lock budget, oversized threshold, degradation mode, progress or cancellation behavior, receipt fields, or responsiveness oracle.
items.impact: Implementations may freeze, truncate, drop fidelity, or emit incompatible receipts while still claiming compliance.
items.builder_discretion: Choose all quantitative budgets and the user-visible degradation/recovery policy.

evidence.exact_quote: - Renderer/scrollback locks are budgeted; oversized recordings degrade with receipts instead of freezing UI.

items.title: Testing GUI commands, layout, and button derivation
items.statement: The GUI exposes six named testing commands, five named panel regions, and receipt-status/artifact-derived watch, cancel, open-receipt, and export enablement rules.

evidence.exact_quote: Testing GUI commands are `cmd.testing.open_panel`, `cmd.testing.watch_run`, `cmd.testing.cancel_run`, `cmd.testing.open_receipt`, `cmd.testing.open_failure`, and `cmd.testing.export_bundle`.

Panel layout contains `run_list`, `active_run_detail`, `failure_list`, `artifact_preview`, and `redaction_notice`. items.impact: GUI and runtime implementations can disagree about when commands are legal and what happens under races or failures.
items.builder_discretion: Infer terminal statuses and invent the run transition graph and command protocol.

items.title: Runtime disabled-to-enabled gate and event
items.statement: Testing enables per adapter only after adapter configuration, an available capability probe, current permissions, required fixtures, and receipt producibility; the enabling event has six named fields.

evidence.exact_quote: Testing remains runtime-disabled until all of the following are true: a target adapter is configured, the target capability probe returns `available`, permission snapshot is current, required fixtures exist, and the test invocation can produce a `TestRunReceipt` without claiming PNC-019 lifecycle certification. The transition event is `testing.runtime_enabled_for_adapter` with fields `adapter_id`, `project_id`, `capability_probe_ref`, `permission_snapshot_id`, `enabled_at_utc`, and `reason_code`.

items.title: No enabled-to-disabled or revocation behavior
items.statement: The spec defines only runtime_disabled-to-enabled; it does not define revocation when an adapter disappears, the capability probe changes, permissions expire, fixtures are removed, or receipt production fails, nor an event or in-flight-run policy for that transition.
items.impact: Testing can remain erroneously enabled after prerequisites cease to hold, with no interoperable cleanup or user-facing recovery behavior.
items.builder_discretion: Invent invalidation detection, disable events, in-flight cancellation, and recovery semantics.

dimension_assessments.summary: Soak scenarios, terminal replay comparisons, UI enablement, and runtime enabling behavior are stated.
Transport soak, terminal corpus/fuzz/replay, GUI surfacing, and adapter enablement capabilities are named.
Invocation and receipt fields are listed, but wire types, invariants, correlation, and reference resolution are missing.
Named field contracts exist but are not implementable interoperable schemas and conflict with later deferred status.
Status values and one enabling transition exist; the run graph and disable/revocation transition do not.
No authority is assigned for state changes, cancellation, artifact access/export, or prerequisite decisions.
Document placement is present, but runtime producer, executor, state, persistence, and reference ownership are absent.
GUI use is implied, but receipt, reference, and enable-event consumers are not enumerated or bound.
Commands, regions, and several button rules are concrete; terminal-state, command lifecycle, preview/export, and redaction behavior remain incomplete.
Graceful oversized-recording degradation is required, but quantitative behavior and prerequisite-loss recovery are absent.
Permission freshness and a redaction notice are mentioned without authorization, scoping, or redaction/export policy.
An enable event is named, but its emitter, delivery, replay, subscribers, and projections are not.
Corpus storage, degradation, watching, cancellation, preview, and export are named without full lifecycle or operational contracts.
Large/giant output and high-frequency snapshots are in scope, but all thresholds, budgets, and performance oracles are missing.
A schema_version field is named without a version value, compatibility rules, or migration behavior.
Replay comparison surfaces and prerequisite categories exist, but soak thresholds, performance budgets, and enablement predicates are not testably defined.
Consequential discretion remains across protocols, state machines, authorities, security, ownership, operations, performance, and event delivery.
Terminal-state meaning is implicit and the same FABLE rows are simultaneously presented as repaired and explicitly deferred.
